name: one_gadget - libc One-Shot RCE Gadgets
description: one_gadget finds 'magic' addresses in a libc build that spawn a shell (execve('/bin/sh',...)) in a single jump, provided certain register/memory constraints hold. Invaluable when you can overwrite one pointer (GOT entry, return address, __malloc_hook) and want instant RCE without a full ROP chain.
notes:
=== INSTALL ===
  gem install one_gadget

=== FIND GADGETS ===
  one_gadget <libc.so.6>
  # prints offsets + the constraints each requires, e.g.:
  #   0xe3b2e execve("/bin/sh", r15, r12)
  #   constraints: [r15]==NULL || r15==NULL , [r12]==NULL || r12==NULL

=== USAGE ===
  # add the chosen offset to the leaked libc base:
  #   one_gadget_addr = libc_base + 0xe3b2e
  # overwrite a hook / return address with it when its constraints are satisfiable

=== RAW / LEVEL ===
  one_gadget <libc.so.6> -l 2     # more (looser) candidates
  one_gadget -b <build_id>        # fetch by libc build id

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  manual system('/bin/sh') ROP chain (ROPgadget + pwntools)
  __free_hook / __malloc_hook overwrite techniques

recommended.note: Resolve libc base in pwntools, then jump to the gadget.
ROPgadget for a full chain when constraints fail.

defense.why_it_works: glibc contains code paths that call execve('/bin/sh') under specific register states. If an attacker can redirect execution to such an address with the right constraints, one pointer overwrite yields a shell.
defense.prerequisites: A libc leak (to defeat ASLR) and a single write/control primitive (hook, GOT, saved return address).
defense.impact: Immediate shell from a single controlled jump, bypassing the need for a multi-gadget ROP chain.
defense.detection: Not detectable as a tool; exploitation surfaces as an unexpected shell child of a service and EDR alerts at runtime.
defense.artifacts: None from the tool; on the target, an execve('/bin/sh') from a daemon is the signal.
defense.prevention: Full ASLR/PIE so libc addresses are unpredictable; FORTIFY and hook-hardening (modern glibc removed __malloc_hook/__free_hook); pointer encryption (PTR_MANGLE); seccomp to forbid execve in services; patch the memory bug that grants the write primitive.
